This report was rendered on `r format(Sys.time(), "%B %d, %Y")`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, dev = "png", dpi = 150)
```

```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

# corrected data (manual corrections pending confirmation by curators)
dat <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds")

# one row per study: metadata are shared by the increased and decreased signatures
studies <- dat |>
  distinct(Study, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, -`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, -`Abundance in Group 1`) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

# colors: health/periodontitis, periodontitis classification, profiling method
# (method colors match the overview figure of the main report; grey is always "not reported")
pal_group <- c(Health = "#2a78d6", Periodontitis = "#eb6834")

class_levels <- c(
  "Chronic periodontitis", "Chronic and aggressive periodontitis", "Aggressive periodontitis",
  "Periodontitis (stage/grade)", "Refractory periodontitis", "Periodontitis (type not specified)"
)
class_short <- c("Chronic", "Chronic + aggressive", "Aggressive", "Stage/grade", "Refractory", "Not specified")
pal_class <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6", "#e87ba4", "#eda100", "#e34948", "grey65"), class_short)

method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                   "PCR", "Other / not reported")
pal_method <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65"), method_levels)

theme_meta <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
theme_set(theme_meta)

studies <- studies |>
  mutate(
    classification = factor(
      class_short[match(`Periodontitis classification`, class_levels)], levels = class_short
    ),
    method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    ) |> factor(levels = method_levels),
    period = cut(Year, c(-Inf, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                 labels = c("1995–2004", "2005–2009", "2010–2014", "2015–2019", "2020–2025"))
  )

# group-level measures in long format
features <- tribble(
  ~feature,   ~label,                          ~mean_col,                        ~sd_col,
  "age",      "Age (years)",                   "age mean",                       "age sd",
  "males",    "Males (%)",                     "percent males",                  NA,
  "smokers",  "Smokers (%)",                   "percent smokers",                NA,
  "pd",       "Probing depth (mm)",            "pocket depth mean (mm)",         "pocket depth sd",
  "cal",      "Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "clinical attachment loss (mm)",  "clinical attachment loss sd",
  "bop",      "Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "bleeding on probing percent",    "bleeding on probing sd",
  "plaque",   "Plaque (% sites)",              "plaque",                         "plaque sd",
  "supp",     "Suppuration (% sites)",         "suppuration percent",            "suppuration sd"
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

long <- pmap_dfr(features, function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
  map_dfr(0:1, function(g) {
    col <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) NA_real_ else studies[[paste("Group", g, x)]]
    num <- if (feature %in% c("males", "smokers")) col(paste("num", feature)) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      Study = studies$Study, feature = feature, label = label,
      group = c("Health", "Periodontitis")[g + 1],
      mean = col(mean_col), sd = col(sd_col),
      n = studies[[paste("Group", g, "sample size")]],
      num = num
    )
  })
}) |>
  # plaque indices (e.g. Silness-Löe 0-3) are not comparable with % sites
  left_join(select(studies, Study, `Plaque measure`), by = "Study") |>
  filter(!is.na(mean), feature != "plaque" | `Plaque measure` %in% "% sites") |>
  select(-`Plaque measure`)

# studies with values for both groups
paired <- long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Study, feature, label), names_from = group,
              values_from = c(mean, sd, n, num)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_Health), !is.na(mean_Periodontitis)) |>
  # smokers excluded from both groups: no contrast
  filter(!(feature == "smokers" & mean_Health == 0 & mean_Periodontitis == 0))

paired_tests <- paired |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    p = wilcox.test(mean_Periodontitis, mean_Health, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", signif(p, 2))))
```

## About this report

This report sets out candidate figures and tables on the metadata of PerioSigDB. It covers how participant and clinical characteristics differ between periodontitis and periodontally healthy groups, and how they vary across studies. Each section is one option, with a short note on what it shows and its caveats. A summary of all options with a recommendation is at the end.

All analyses use the **corrected** dataset (`output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds`). Its manual corrections are pending confirmation by the curators; see `output/manual_corrections.csv`. The unit of analysis is the **study** (n = `r nrow(studies)`), because metadata are recorded once per study and shared by its increased and decreased signatures. Group 0 is the periodontally healthy group and Group 1 the periodontitis group. Health groups are not uniform:

- Studies 298, 153 and 155 include gingivitis subjects in Group 0.
- Studies 1752, 1818 and 1897 use periodontitis-resistant adults aged 65 and over.

# Data availability

## Option 1: Metadata completeness heatmap

```{r completeness}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Reporting of metadata across studies. Each column is a study, ordered by publication year; each row is a field. Group-level fields are shaded by whether they are reported for both groups, one group, or neither. Plaque counts as reported only when given as % of sites. The percentage after each field is the share of studies reporting it for both groups (group-level fields) or at all (study-level fields)."

study_fields <- tibble(
  Study = studies$Study,
  `Profiling method` = studies$method != "Other / not reported",
  `16S variable region` = !is.na(studies$`16S variable region`),
  `Periodontitis classification` = studies$classification != "Not specified",
  `Systemic condition` = !is.na(studies$`Systemic condition`),
  `Group 0 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 0 definition`),
  `Group 1 definition` = !is.na(studies$`Group 1 definition`)
) |>
  pivot_longer(-Study, names_to = "field", values_to = "reported") |>
  mutate(status = ifelse(reported, "Reported", "Not reported"), type = "Study")

size_fields <- studies |>
  transmute(Study, n0 = !is.na(`Group 0 sample size`), n1 = !is.na(`Group 1 sample size`)) |>
  mutate(field = "Sample size")

group_fields <- long |>
  distinct(Study, label, group) |>
  count(Study, field = as.character(label), name = "groups") |>
  complete(Study = studies$Study, field = levels(features$label), fill = list(groups = 0)) |>
  bind_rows(transmute(size_fields, Study, field, groups = n0 + n1)) |>
  mutate(
    status = c("Neither group", "One group", "Both groups")[groups + 1],
    type = "Group"
  )

completeness <- bind_rows(group_fields, study_fields) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(
    Study = fct_reorder(Study, Year, .fun = min),
    complete = status %in% c("Both groups", "Reported")
  ) |>
  mutate(field_label = paste0(field, " (", round(100 * mean(complete)), "%)"), .by = field)

field_order <- completeness |>
  summarise(pct = mean(complete), type = first(type), .by = field_label) |>
  arrange(type == "Study", pct) |>
  pull(field_label)

pal_status <- c(
  "Both groups" = "#2a78d6", "One group" = "#9ec5f4", "Neither group" = "#f0efec",
  "Reported" = "#256abf", "Not reported" = "#f0efec"
)

ggplot(completeness, aes(x = Study, y = factor(field_label, levels = field_order), fill = status)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_status, breaks = c("Both groups", "One group", "Neither group")) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = NULL, breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Studies (ordered by publication year →)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank())
```

**Shows:** how complete each field is, and whether reporting improved over time. For example, recent studies more often give a periodontitis stage/grade. This is useful as a supplementary figure in a resource paper, and it sets expectations for every other option below.

**Caveat:** "Not reported" can also mean "not entered". Systemic condition was not extracted for most studies in the original overview sheet.

# Health vs periodontitis

## Option 2: Paired study-level comparison

```{r paired-slopes}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Health vs periodontitis within each study. Grey lines join the two groups of one study; large points are medians across studies. n is the number of studies reporting the measure for both groups; p is from a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies."

medians <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(label, group))

strip_labels <- paired_tests |>
  arrange(label) |>
  mutate(strip = paste0(label, "\nn = ", studies, ", ", p_label)) |>
  mutate(strip = factor(strip, levels = strip)) |>
  select(label, strip)

long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  left_join(strip_labels, by = "label") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
            aes(y = median, group = 1), color = "grey15", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
             aes(y = median, fill = group), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 4, stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~strip, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

**Shows:** the size and consistency of the health–periodontitis difference for each measure, and how much individual studies vary around it. Clinical measures separate almost every study. The demographic measures show the imbalances between groups: periodontitis groups tend to be older and to smoke more.

**Caveat:** each study counts equally, regardless of its sample size.

## Option 3: Summary table ("Table 1")

```{r table1}
pooled <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  filter(!is.na(n)) |>
  summarise(
    subjects = sum(n),
    pooled_mean = sum(n * mean) / sum(n),
    .by = c(label, group)
  )

iqr_fmt <- function(x, digits) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f]"), q[2], q[1], q[3])
}

table1 <- paired |>
  mutate(digits = ifelse(feature %in% c("pd", "cal"), 2, 1)) |>
  summarise(
    Studies = n(),
    Health = iqr_fmt(mean_Health, first(digits)),
    Periodontitis = iqr_fmt(mean_Periodontitis, first(digits)),
    Difference = iqr_fmt(mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health, first(digits)),
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  left_join(select(paired_tests, feature, p_label), by = "feature") |>
  left_join(
    pooled |>
      mutate(pooled_mean = sprintf(ifelse(grepl("mm", label), "%.2f", "%.1f"), pooled_mean)) |>
      pivot_wider(id_cols = label, names_from = group, values_from = c(pooled_mean, subjects)),
    by = "label"
  ) |>
  arrange(label) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label, Studies,
    Health, Periodontitis, Difference, `Paired test` = p_label,
    `Health ` = paste0(pooled_mean_Health, " (", subjects_Health, ")"),
    `Periodontitis ` = paste0(pooled_mean_Periodontitis, " (", subjects_Periodontitis, ")")
  )

table1 |>
  kbl(align = "lcccccccc",
      caption = "Health and periodontitis groups across studies reporting each measure for both groups. Study-level columns give the median [IQR] of study means; the paired test is a Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies. Pooled columns weight each study mean by its group size (number of subjects in brackets).") |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Study means, median [IQR]" = 3, " " = 1, "Pooled mean (subjects)" = 2)) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE)
```

**Shows:** the conventional "Table 1" in compact form, with both the between-study spread and a subject-weighted pooled mean. It pairs naturally with Option 2 or Option 4.

**Caveat:** the pooled means ignore within-study variance and differences in measurement protocol (e.g. full-mouth vs sampled sites).

## Option 4: Pooled effect sizes

```{r effect-sizes}
# Hedges' g (continuous) and log odds ratios (males, smokers) per study,
# pooled with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model
hedges_g <- function(m1, s1, n1, m0, s0, n0) {
  sp <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * s1^2 + (n0 - 1) * s0^2) / (n1 + n0 - 2))
  g <- (1 - 3 / (4 * (n1 + n0) - 9)) * (m1 - m0) / sp
  tibble(yi = g, vi = (n1 + n0) / (n1 * n0) + g^2 / (2 * (n1 + n0)))
}

log_or <- function(x1, n1, x0, n0) {
  cc <- ifelse(x1 == 0 | x0 == 0 | x1 == n1 | x0 == n0, 0.5, 0)
  a <- x1 + cc; b <- n1 - x1 + cc; c <- x0 + cc; d <- n0 - x0 + cc
  tibble(yi = log(a * d / (b * c)), vi = 1 / a + 1 / b + 1 / c + 1 / d)
}

dersimonian_laird <- function(yi, vi) {
  w <- 1 / vi
  k <- length(yi)
  q <- sum(w * (yi - sum(w * yi) / sum(w))^2)
  tau2 <- max(0, (q - (k - 1)) / (sum(w) - sum(w^2) / sum(w)))
  ws <- 1 / (vi + tau2)
  est <- sum(ws * yi) / sum(ws)
  se <- sqrt(1 / sum(ws))
  tibble(k = k, est = est, lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se,
         i2 = ifelse(q > 0, max(0, (q - (k - 1)) / q), 0))
}

per_study <- bind_rows(
  paired |>
    filter(!feature %in% c("males", "smokers"),
           !is.na(sd_Health), !is.na(sd_Periodontitis), !is.na(n_Health), !is.na(n_Periodontitis),
           sd_Health > 0 | sd_Periodontitis > 0) |>
    mutate(hedges_g(mean_Periodontitis, sd_Periodontitis, n_Periodontitis,
                    mean_Health, sd_Health, n_Health), scale = "Hedges' g"),
  paired |>
    filter(feature %in% c("males", "smokers"), !is.na(num_Health), !is.na(num_Periodontitis),
           # no contrast when both groups exclude smokers
           num_Health + num_Periodontitis > 0) |>
    mutate(log_or(num_Periodontitis, n_Periodontitis, num_Health, n_Health), scale = "Odds ratio")
)

pooled_effects <- per_study |>
  summarise(dersimonian_laird(yi, vi), .by = c(label, scale)) |>
  mutate(across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ ifelse(scale == "Odds ratio", exp(.x), .x)))
```

```{r effect-sizes-fig}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Pooled difference between periodontitis and health groups (random-effects meta-analysis across studies, 95% CI). Left: standardized mean difference (Hedges' g) for continuous measures. Right: odds ratio of being male or a smoker in the periodontitis group. k = number of studies; I² = share of variability due to between-study heterogeneity."

effect_plot <- function(d, xlab, ref, log = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = est, y = fct_rev(label))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8, color = pal_group[["Periodontitis"]]) +
    geom_point(size = 3, color = pal_group[["Periodontitis"]]) +
    geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = sprintf("k = %d, I² = %d%%", k, round(100 * i2))),
              hjust = -0.1, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.35)))
  if (log) p <- p + scale_x_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.9)))
  p
}

effect_plot(filter(pooled_effects, scale == "Hedges' g"), "Hedges' g (periodontitis − health)", 0) +
  effect_plot(filter(pooled_effects, scale == "Odds ratio"), "Odds ratio (periodontitis vs health)", 1, log = TRUE) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))
```

**Shows:** one standardized number per measure, so measures on different scales can be compared directly. The I² values make the heterogeneity explicit, and the odds ratios make the age, sex and smoking confounding concrete.

**Caveats:**

- This only includes studies that report SDs (or counts).
- Standardized effects of clinical measures are very large, because healthy groups are defined by low PD, CAL and BOP. The effect partly reflects case definitions rather than biology.
- Some SDs come from SEM conversions or pooled subgroups (see `manual_corrections.csv`).

# Variation within periodontitis groups

## Option 5: Disease severity by periodontitis classification

```{r within-perio}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values across studies, by periodontitis classification (one point per study). Bars are medians. Smokers at 0% are mostly studies that excluded smokers."

within <- long |>
  filter(group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("age", "smokers", "pd", "cal", "bop")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, classification), by = "Study")

ggplot(within, aes(x = classification, y = mean, color = classification)) +
  geom_quasirandom(size = 1.8, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey15") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_class) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

**Shows:** whether "periodontitis" means comparable disease across studies. Aggressive-periodontitis studies are younger and have deeper pockets, while unspecified and stage/grade studies span a wide severity range.

**Caveat:** some groups have few studies (e.g. refractory n = 1). PD/CAL are sometimes from sampled sites only, which inflates them.

## Option 6: Trends over publication year

```{r trends}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values by publication year (one point per study). Grey lines are linear trends with 95% confidence bands."

within |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = mean)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "grey40", fill = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = pal_group[["Periodontitis"]], color = "white", size = 2.4, stroke = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = NULL)
```

**Shows:** whether the periodontitis cohorts recruited have changed over three decades of publications (e.g. older patients and higher BOP in recent studies). This is relevant to whether older and newer signatures are comparable.

**Caveat:** publication year is confounded with profiling method, since sequencing replaced hybridization and PCR over the same period, so a time trend cannot be separated from a method effect.

# Study characteristics

## Option 7: Periodontitis classification over time and by method

```{r classification}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Periodontitis classification of studies by publication period (share of studies; counts in bars). (B) Number of studies by classification and profiling method."

pA <- studies |>
  count(period, classification) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), .by = period) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = fct_rev(period), fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop > 0.06, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            color = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

pB <- studies |>
  count(classification, method) |>
  complete(classification, method, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = fct_rev(classification), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, ""), color = n > 12), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab", guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
```

**Shows:** the shift from the 1999 chronic/aggressive classification to the 2018 stage/grade system, and which diagnosis types each profiling method has studied. This is useful context for stratifying signatures.

**Caveat:** "Not specified" is large. Many older studies define periodontitis only by PD/CAL thresholds.

## Option 8: Systemic condition of participants

```{r systemic}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Systemic condition of participants (number of studies). Not recorded: not extracted in the overview sheet."

studies |>
  mutate(systemic = case_when(
    is.na(`Systemic condition`) ~ "Not recorded",
    `Systemic condition` == "systemically healthy" ~ "Systemically healthy",
    .default = str_to_sentence(`Systemic condition`)
  )) |>
  count(systemic) |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      systemic == "Not recorded" ~ "Not recorded",
      systemic == "Systemically healthy" ~ "Systemically healthy",
      .default = "Includes systemic disease"
    ),
    systemic = fct_reorder(systemic, n)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = systemic, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Systemically healthy" = "#2a78d6", "Includes systemic disease" = "#eb6834",
                               "Not recorded" = "grey65")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL)
```

**Shows:** which signatures come from populations with comorbidities (rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, COPD, HIV), so they can be flagged or excluded in sensitivity analyses.

**Caveat:** this is unknown for about half the studies until the curators fill it in. It might work better as a table than a figure.

## Option 9: Sample size by profiling method

```{r sample-size}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Total participants per study (health + periodontitis, log scale) by publication year, colored by profiling method."

studies |>
  mutate(total = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`) |>
  filter(!is.na(total)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = total)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = method), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 3, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_method) +
  labs(x = "Publication year", y = "Participants (log scale)")
```

**Shows:** sequencing studies are typically small, while checkerboard and PCR studies include hundreds of subjects. This is relevant for weighting signatures, or for reading differences between methods.

**Caveat:** participants are not samples. Many studies analyse several sites per subject (pooled or not).

## Option 10: Group imbalance in age and smoking

```{r imbalance}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Difference between periodontitis and health groups in mean age (x) and % smokers (y), one point per study reporting both for both groups (studies excluding smokers from both groups omitted). Studies with the largest differences are labelled."

imbalance <- paired |>
  filter(feature %in% c("age", "smokers")) |>
  transmute(Study, feature, diff = mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = feature, values_from = diff) |>
  filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(smokers)) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, classification), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(label = ifelse(abs(smokers) > 40 | abs(age) > 25 | age < -5, sub("Study ", "", Study), NA))

ggplot(imbalance, aes(x = age, y = smokers)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = classification), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 3, stroke = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 3, color = "grey25", min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  labs(x = "Age difference, years (periodontitis − health)",
       y = "Smokers difference, percentage points") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

**Shows:** age and smoking imbalances in a single view. Most studies have older periodontitis groups and many also have more smokers. (The periodontitis-resistant cohorts with older controls, 1752/1818/1897, don't report smoking for controls, so they are not shown; their age inversion is visible in Option 2.) These are the two main confounders of periodontitis signatures.

**Caveat:** many studies don't report smoking for both groups, often because smokers were excluded entirely.

# Metadata and signature content

## Option 11: Signature content by study characteristics

```{r signature-content}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Number of taxa in the increased signature vs the probing-depth difference between groups (log scale), colored by profiling method. (B) Share of studies, by periodontitis classification, whose increased signature includes each red-complex species. The denominator is all studies with an increased signature, including targeted assays that may not have tested the species."

sigs <- dat |>
  filter(`Abundance in Group 1` == "increased") |>
  mutate(
    size = lengths(`MetaPhlAn taxon names`),
    taxa = map_chr(`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, paste, collapse = ";")
  ) |>
  select(Study, size, taxa) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, method, classification), by = "Study")

pd_gap <- paired |>
  filter(feature == "pd") |>
  transmute(Study, pd_gap = mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health)

pA <- sigs |>
  inner_join(pd_gap, by = "Study") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pd_gap, y = size)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = method), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 2.8, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_method) +
  labs(x = "Probing depth difference, mm (periodontitis − health)",
       y = "Taxa in increased signature", tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

red_complex <- c("Porphyromonas gingivalis", "Tannerella forsythia", "Treponema denticola")
pB <- map_dfr(red_complex, function(sp) {
  sigs |>
    summarise(studies = n(), share = mean(grepl(sp, taxa, fixed = TRUE)), .by = classification) |>
    mutate(species = sp)
}) |>
  mutate(class_n = fct_rev(fct_reorder(paste0(classification, " (n=", studies, ")"), as.integer(classification)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = class_n, fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~species, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Studies reporting species as increased", y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold.italic"))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.6))
```

**Shows:** the link from metadata to the microbial results. Does a larger clinical contrast give larger signatures? Do the classic pathogens appear consistently across diagnosis types? This is the most novel option and leads into stratified analyses of the signatures.

**Caveats:**

- This is exploratory: signature size depends mostly on the profiling method's coverage.
- Without per-study lists of the taxa that were assessed, absence from a signature can't be told apart from "not tested".
- The species-assessed field in the raw sheets could supply this if it were cleaned.

# Comparison with BugSigDB

```{r bugsigdb-load}
# BugSigDB export (cached by bugsigdbr; version date from its message)
bsdb_version <- NA_character_
bsdb <- withCallingHandlers(
  bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB(),
  warning = function(w) {
    bsdb_version <<- sub(".*from ", "", conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
if (is.na(bsdb_version)) bsdb_version <- format(Sys.Date())

oral_sites <- "plaque|saliva|mouth|oral|tongue|gingiv|throat|oroph|tonsil|buccal|cheek"

# BugSigDB without its periodontitis signatures (PerioSigDB is the reference for those)
bsdb_other <- filter(bsdb, !grepl("periodont", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE))

db_levels <- c("PerioSigDB", "BugSigDB")
pal_db <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6"), db_levels)

# genera of the taxa in a signature (taxa above genus rank are dropped)
genera <- function(x) unique(sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", x[grepl("g__", x)]))

sig_genera <- function(d) {
  tibble(
    sig = seq_len(nrow(d)), Condition = d$Condition, `Body site` = d$`Body site`,
    direction = d$`Abundance in Group 1`, taxon = map(d$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)
  ) |>
    unnest(taxon)
}
```

PerioSigDB uses BugSigDB's format, so its signatures can be set against the rest of the microbiome literature. These options use the BugSigDB export of `r bsdb_version`, with `r n_distinct(bsdb$PMID)` studies and `r nrow(bsdb)` signatures across all conditions and body sites. BugSigDB's own periodontitis signatures (`r nrow(bsdb) - nrow(bsdb_other)`) are excluded throughout.

## Option 12: Profiling methods and taxonomic resolution

```{r bsdb-methods}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "(A) Profiling method of signatures. (B) Taxonomic rank of the taxa in signatures. BugSigDB includes all conditions and body sites except periodontitis."

method_of <- function(type, platform) {
  case_when(
    type == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
    type == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
    type %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
    platform == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
    .default = "Other / not reported"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)
}

methods_db <- bind_rows(
  dat |> transmute(db = "PerioSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`)),
  bsdb_other |> transmute(db = "BugSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`))
) |>
  count(db, method) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

rank_names <- c(s = "Species", g = "Genus", f = "Family", o = "Order", c = "Class", p = "Phylum", k = "Kingdom")
pal_rank <- c(Species = "#184f95", Genus = "#3987e5", Family = "#86b6ef", Higher = "#cde2fb")

ranks_db <- bind_rows(
  tibble(db = "PerioSigDB", taxon = unlist(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`)),
  tibble(db = "BugSigDB", taxon = unlist(bsdb_other$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`))
) |>
  mutate(
    rank = rank_names[substr(sub(".*[|]", "", taxon), 1, 1)],
    rank = factor(ifelse(rank %in% c("Species", "Genus", "Family"), rank, "Higher"), levels = names(pal_rank))
  ) |>
  count(db, rank) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

stack_bar <- function(d, fill, pal, tag) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = db, fill = {{ fill }})) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.06, scales::percent(prop, 1), "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}

stack_bar(methods_db, method, pal_method, "A") +
  stack_bar(ranks_db, rank, pal_rank, "B") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```

**Shows:** PerioSigDB is dominated by targeted assays (checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization and PCR) that report named species, whereas BugSigDB is mostly 16S and shotgun sequencing reported at genus level. This is the main structural difference between the two databases. It is why Option 14 compares them at genus level.

## Option 13: Metadata captured by each database

```{r bsdb-fields}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Share of signatures with each field filled in, by database. BugSigDB records statistical methods and diversity; PerioSigDB records participant and clinical characteristics."

filled <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) return(lengths(x) > 0)
  !is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA"))
}
field_share <- function(d, db, fields) {
  tibble(
    db = db, field = fields,
    share = map_dbl(fields, \(f) if (f %in% names(d)) mean(filled(d[[f]])) else NA_real_)
  )
}

shared_fields <- c("Group 1 definition", "Group 0 sample size", "Group 1 sample size",
                   "Sequencing type", "16S variable region", "Sequencing platform", "Location of subjects")
bsdb_fields <- c("Statistical test", "Significance threshold", "MHT correction", "LDA Score above",
                 "Matched on", "Confounders controlled for", "Antibiotics exclusion", "Shannon", "Richness")
perio_fields <- c("Group 0 definition", "Periodontitis classification", "Systemic condition",
                  "Group 1 age mean", "Group 1 percent males", "Group 1 percent smokers",
                  "Group 1 pocket depth mean (mm)", "Group 1 clinical attachment loss (mm)",
                  "Group 1 bleeding on probing percent", "Group 1 plaque")
all_fields <- c(shared_fields, bsdb_fields, perio_fields)
field_label <- function(x) sub("^Group 0 ", "Health ", sub("^Group 1 ", "Periodontitis ", x))

fields_db <- bind_rows(
  field_share(dat, "PerioSigDB", all_fields),
  field_share(bsdb_other, "BugSigDB", all_fields)
) |>
  mutate(
    # classification "not specified" counts as missing
    share = ifelse(db == "PerioSigDB" & field == "Periodontitis classification",
                   mean(dat$`Periodontitis classification` != "Periodontitis (type not specified)"), share),
    field_type = case_when(
      field %in% shared_fields ~ "Both databases",
      field %in% bsdb_fields ~ "BugSigDB only",
      .default = "PerioSigDB only"
    ),
    field = factor(field_label(field), levels = rev(field_label(all_fields))),
    db = factor(db, levels = db_levels)
  )

ggplot(fields_db, aes(x = db, y = field)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = share, fill = db), shape = 21, color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(share), "–", scales::percent(share, 1))),
            nudge_x = 0.22, hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(field_type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_db, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.7))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

**Shows:** the two databases record complementary metadata. PerioSigDB adds participant and clinical characteristics that BugSigDB has no fields for. BugSigDB records the statistical test, significance threshold, multiple-testing correction and matching, which PerioSigDB lacks. Adding those fields to PerioSigDB would make it fully importable into BugSigDB.

**Caveats:**

- A filled field is not necessarily a complete one (e.g. "Matched on" can list only some of the variables).
- PerioSigDB's lower sequencing type completeness is mostly checkerboard hybridization, which has no sequencing type in BugSigDB's vocabulary.

## Option 14: PerioSigDB taxa across other conditions

```{r bsdb-conditions-data}
# genera with the most consistent direction in PerioSigDB: exact binomial test of increased vs
# decreased signatures against 50% (as for taxa in the main report), then how often the top 20
# in each direction appear in BugSigDB signatures of the same direction for each other condition
n_sig_dir <- table(dat$`Abundance in Group 1`)

perio_tests <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    signatures = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased")
  )

perio_genera <- perio_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20, by = direction) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05",
      p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05 (not FDR)",
      .default = "Not significant"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)", "Not significant"))
  )

# body site group of each signature (signatures listing sites in several groups are "mixed")
gi_sites <- paste0("feces|colon|colorectal|intestin|caecum|cecum|rectum|ileum|jejunum|duoden|stomach|",
                   "gastric|esophag|meconium|digestive|bile|rumen|cloaca|midgut|proventriculus")
site_group <- function(sites) {
  map_chr(strsplit(sites, ","), function(x) {
    groups <- unique(case_when(
      grepl(oral_sites, x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "oral",
      grepl(gi_sites, x, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "gastrointestinal",
      .default = "other"
    ))
    if (length(groups) == 1) groups else "mixed"
  })
}

# disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only: Group 0 is a control group and Group 1 is not.
# This drops body site, time point, treatment arm, diet and reversed comparisons, which BugSigDB
# also files under the study's condition
control_names <- paste0("control|healthy|\\bhealth\\b|normal|\\bnon[- ]?|without|negative|unaffected|",
                        "\\bHC\\b|\\bNC\\b|cognitively (intact|unimpaired)|^no\\b|-free\\b|peritumo|adjacent|benign")
bsdb_cc <- bsdb_other |>
  filter(grepl(control_names, `Group 0 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl(control_names, `Group 1 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         `Abundance in Group 1` %in% c("increased", "decreased"))

# count each study once per condition, direction and body site group: the units below are
# study-level, and a genus is in a unit if it is in any of the study's signatures in that unit
bsdb_cc_sigs <- tibble(
  sig = seq_len(nrow(bsdb_cc)), bsdb_id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study,
  Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition, direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  oral = grepl(oral_sites, bsdb_cc$`Body site`, ignore.case = TRUE),
  site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`)
) |>
  mutate(unit = as.integer(factor(paste(Study, Condition, direction, site_group, sep = "|"))))

bsdb_sigs <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  summarise(oral = any(oral), .by = c(unit, Study, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  rename(sig = unit)

bsdb_genera <- sig_genera(bsdb_cc) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_cc_sigs, sig, unit), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(sig = unit, direction, taxon)

# left panel: PerioSigDB signatures with the genus increased (right) and decreased (left)
perio_panel <- function(top, genus_levels) {
  perio_counts <- top |>
    select(taxon, increased, decreased, significance) |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))

  max_n <- max(abs(perio_counts$n))
  ggplot(perio_counts, aes(x = n, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = significance), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = distinct(top, taxon, fdr),
              aes(x = -max_n * 1.05, label = ifelse(fdr < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", fdr))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.5, color = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = NULL) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                       drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = scales::breaks_extended()(c(-max_n, max_n)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures\n(left: FDR)", y = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 1), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1)) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}

# top bar: share of each column's signatures from oral body sites
oral_panel <- function(columns) {
  ggplot(columns, aes(x = col, y = oral)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 0.7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Oral sites") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}

# one-sided test of a genus being in a condition's signatures more often than in other conditions'
# signatures from the same body site group; strata without both are uninformative and dropped
site_matched_p <- function(condition, genus, sigs, hits) {
  d <- sigs |>
    mutate(in_condition = Condition == condition, has_genus = sig %in% hits$sig[hits$taxon == genus])
  informative <- d |>
    summarise(ok = any(in_condition) & any(!in_condition), .by = site_group) |>
    filter(ok) |>
    pull(site_group)
  if (!length(informative)) return(NA_real_)
  d <- filter(d, site_group %in% informative)
  tab <- table(factor(d$in_condition, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$has_genus, c(TRUE, FALSE)),
               factor(d$site_group))
  if (dim(tab)[3] == 1) {
    fisher.test(tab[, , 1], alternative = "greater")$p.value
  } else {
    mantelhaen.test(tab, exact = TRUE, alternative = "greater")$p.value
  }
}

# match_site = TRUE compares each condition with other signatures from the same body site group
# (exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site group) instead of all other signatures
condition_heatmap <- function(dir, n_conditions = 15, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)

  # enrichment of each genus in each condition's signatures vs all other BugSigDB signatures of
  # this direction: one-sided Fisher's exact test, BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
  condition_sizes <- sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)

  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")

  enrichment <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, taxon, name = "n") |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = condition_sizes$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(
      n = coalesce(n, 0L), with_genus = coalesce(with_genus, 0L),
      share = n / signatures,
      p = if (match_site) {
        map2_dbl(Condition, taxon, site_matched_p, sigs = sigs, hits = hits)
      } else {
        pmap_dbl(list(n, signatures, with_genus), function(a, n_cond, n_genus) {
          fisher.test(matrix(c(a, n_cond - a, n_genus - a, nrow(sigs) - n_cond - n_genus + a), 2),
                      alternative = "greater")$p.value
        })
      },
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )

  # conditions with the most significantly enriched genera (ties: smallest combined p-value)
  conditions <- enrichment |>
    summarise(n_enriched = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), score = sum(-log10(p), na.rm = TRUE),
              .by = c(Condition, signatures, oral)) |>
    arrange(desc(n_enriched), desc(score)) |>
    slice_head(n = n_conditions)

  # first column: all BugSigDB signatures of this direction (baseline)
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(sigs), oral = mean(sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  baseline <- tibble(taxon = top$taxon) |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    transmute(Condition = "All BugSigDB", taxon, share = coalesce(with_genus, 0L) / nrow(sigs), fdr = NA_real_)

  shares <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
    select(Condition, taxon, share, fdr) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05)

  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)
  high <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"

  p_heat <- ggplot(shares, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = share)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(shares, enriched), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(enriched | share >= 0.1, round(100 * share), ""),
                  color = share > 0.45, fontface = ifelse(enriched, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.7) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA),
                        name = "BugSigDB\nstudies") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey20", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         caption = if (match_site) {
           "Outlined, bold: enriched vs other studies from the same body site group (exact CMH test, FDR < 0.05)"
         } else {
           "Outlined, bold: enriched vs all other BugSigDB studies (Fisher's exact test, FDR < 0.05)"
         }) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it increased vs decreased against 50% (the same test as for PerioSigDB),
# BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
direction_heatmap <- function(dir, n_conditions = 15, min_sigs = 5) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)

  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon) |>
    left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, direction), by = "sig") |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased"))

  condition_sizes <- bsdb_sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)

  direction_test <- function(d) {
    d |>
      mutate(
        n = increased + decreased,
        same = if (dir == "increased") increased else decreased,
        share_same = same / n,
        p = map2_dbl(same, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
        fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
      )
  }
  count_directions <- function(d, ...) {
    d |>
      count(..., taxon, direction) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
      (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                    decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))()
  }

  tests <- hits |>
    filter(Condition %in% condition_sizes$Condition) |>
    count_directions(Condition) |>
    direction_test()

  baseline <- hits |>
    count_directions() |>
    direction_test() |>
    mutate(Condition = "All BugSigDB")

  # conditions with the most genera significantly in the same direction as periodontitis
  conditions <- tests |>
    summarise(n_consistent = sum(fdr < 0.05 & share_same > 0.5),
              score = sum(-log10(p[share_same > 0.5])), .by = Condition) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    arrange(desc(n_consistent), desc(score)) |>
    slice_head(n = n_conditions)

  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(bsdb_sigs), oral = mean(bsdb_sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  cells <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(tests, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = columns$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(
      significant = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
      # too few signatures to show a direction
      few = !is.na(n) & n < 3,
      share_plot = ifelse(few, NA, share_same),
      label = ifelse(!is.na(n) & !few, paste0(same, "/", n), "")
    )

  same_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"
  opposite_col <- if (dir == "increased") "#1c5cab" else "#c2410c"

  p_heat <- ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = share_plot)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, few), fill = "grey85", color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, significant), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.4, color = "grey15") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = opposite_col, mid = "#f0efec", high = same_col, midpoint = 0.5,
                         limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, na.value = "white",
                         name = paste0("Studies\nreporting it\n", dir)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
         caption = paste0("Cell labels: studies with the genus ", dir, " / all studies with the genus.\n",
                          "Outlined, bold: binomial test FDR < 0.05. Grey: 1-2 studies. White: genus not reported.")) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}
```

These figures ask: **the taxa that PerioSigDB most consistently links to periodontitis, where else do they turn up in the microbiome literature?** Each figure uses either taxa increased in periodontitis or taxa decreased (health-associated). Four versions answer the question with different tests, so you can compare them.

**BugSigDB data used (all versions):**

- **Disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only.** A signature is kept if its Group 0 name looks like a control (e.g. "healthy", "control", "normal", "non-…", "without …", adjacent or benign tissue) and its Group 1 name does not. BugSigDB files every comparison in a study under the study's condition, including body site comparisons, time points, treatment arms, diet groups and comparisons with the groups reversed. These would otherwise show up as condition effects; phenylketonuria and cognitive impairment did so in earlier versions of this figure. This keeps `r nrow(bsdb_cc)` of `r nrow(bsdb_other)` non-periodontitis signatures, from `r n_distinct(bsdb_cc$Study)` studies.
- **Each study counted once.** The unit is a study's signatures for one condition, direction and body site group (see Version A2), and a genus counts as present if it is in any of them. A study with several near-identical signatures (e.g. for subgroups) therefore counts once. All numbers in brackets and percentages below are numbers of such **studies**.

Versions A, A2 and B are heatmaps that share two parts:

- **Rows (left panel):** the 20 genera with the most consistent direction in PerioSigDB, ordered by p-value.
    - For each genus, an exact binomial test compares the number of PerioSigDB signatures reporting it as increased with the number reporting it as decreased, against an even 50/50 split. This is the same test the main report uses for taxa.
    - The bars show those two counts (orange: increased in periodontitis, to the right; blue: decreased, to the left).
    - Bar opacity marks significance after Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all genera, and the number on the far left is the FDR. Genera that are not significant are still shown to make up 20 per direction.
    - PerioSigDB taxa are mostly species, so they are aggregated to genus to match BugSigDB, where genus is the most common rank (Option 12).
- **Top bar (grey):** the share of each column's studies from oral body sites (plaque, saliva, tongue, mucosa and so on). This separates oral conditions, where the genera are expected, from distant sites such as the gut, where finding oral genera is more notable.

### Version A: enrichment compared with other conditions

Asks: *is the genus reported in this direction more often in this condition than in other conditions?* This measures how **specific** a genus is to a condition.

- **First column, "All BugSigDB" (left of the black line):** the share of *all* BugSigDB studies of the same direction (any condition, excluding periodontitis) that include each genus. This is the baseline, i.e. how common the genus is in microbiome signatures in general.
- **Other columns:** BugSigDB conditions, each with its number of studies of that direction in brackets. Each cell is the share of that condition's studies that include the genus.
    - Each cell is tested for **enrichment**: is the genus in this condition's studies more often than in all other BugSigDB studies of the same direction? The test is a one-sided Fisher's exact test, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all genus × condition tests in that figure (every condition with at least 5 studies, not only those shown).
    - Cells with FDR < 0.05 are outlined and their percentage is in bold.
    - Other cells show their percentage only when it is 10% or more.
- **Which conditions are shown:** the 15 conditions with the most significantly enriched genera, ties broken by the smallest combined p-values, among conditions with at least 5 studies of that direction.

```{r bsdb-conditions-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most often increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and their share of BugSigDB signatures of taxa increased in other conditions. See the text above for how to read the figure."
condition_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-conditions-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most often decreased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and their share of BugSigDB signatures of taxa decreased in other conditions. See the text above for how to read the figure."
condition_heatmap("decreased")
```

**Shows (Version A):**

- **Increased:** `r sum(perio_tests$direction == "increased" & perio_tests$fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)` genera are significantly more often increased than decreased in PerioSigDB (FDR < 0.05). They include the red complex (*Tannerella*, *Treponema*, *Porphyromonas*) and newer periodontal pathogens such as *Filifactor*, *Desulfobulbus* and *Fretibacterium*. These genera are uncommon across BugSigDB as a whole (baseline column).
    - Colorectal cancer, sampled almost entirely outside the mouth, is the clearest result. *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium* are each enriched (39–56% of its studies), consistent with oral–gut translocation.
    - Rheumatoid arthritis is enriched for *Treponema*. Oral cancers and smoking have high shares of several periodontal genera but, with only 5–19 studies each, do not reach significance.
- **Decreased:** only `r sum(perio_tests$direction == "decreased" & perio_tests$fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)` genera reach FDR < 0.05 in PerioSigDB (*Rothia*, *Corynebacterium*, *Haemophilus*, *Gemella*, *Lautropia*), partly because PerioSigDB has fewer decreased signatures and targeted panels rarely include commensals. In BugSigDB, the only significant cell is *Gemella* in smoking. Smoking and the oral cancers have high shares of several commensals, which suggests a shared loss of commensals in oral dysbiosis, but this is not significant.

This positions PerioSigDB as a reference set of "oral pathobiont" and "oral commensal" signatures for the rest of BugSigDB.

### Version A2: enrichment compared with other conditions from the same body sites

Asks the same question as Version A, but compares each condition only with other conditions' studies **from the same body site group**. Oral genera are far more common in oral samples than in feces, and most of BugSigDB is fecal. Version A therefore favours conditions sampled in the mouth and understates oral genera in gut conditions; A2 removes that bias.

- Each BugSigDB signature is assigned a body site group from its body sites (a study's signatures in different groups form separate units):
    - **Oral:** mouth, saliva, dental plaque, tongue, mucosa, oropharynx and so on (as for the grey top bar).
    - **Gastrointestinal:** feces, colon, intestine, stomach, oesophagus and so on.
    - **Other:** all remaining sites, e.g. vagina, skin, nasopharynx, lung.
    - **Mixed:** signatures listing sites in more than one group form their own group.
- Each cell is tested with a one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test stratified by body site group, i.e. a Fisher's exact test within each group, combined across groups. A condition with 70% oral and 30% fecal studies is therefore compared with an oral background for its oral studies and a fecal background for its fecal ones. Groups where no other condition has studies add no information and are dropped.
- Everything else (cell colours and numbers, outlines, FDR correction, choice of conditions, the "All BugSigDB" column) is as in Version A. The "All BugSigDB" column is still unmatched and is only a rough reference.

```{r bsdb-site-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "As Version A (taxa increased in periodontitis), but each condition is compared with other conditions' signatures from the same body site group."
condition_heatmap("increased", match_site = TRUE)
```

```{r bsdb-site-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "As Version A (taxa decreased in periodontitis), but each condition is compared with other conditions' signatures from the same body site group."
condition_heatmap("decreased", match_site = TRUE)
```

**Shows (Version A2):**

- **Increased:** only colorectal cancer remains. Compared only with other gastrointestinal studies, *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium* are all still significantly enriched.
- **Oral conditions:** rheumatoid arthritis, oral cancers and smoking have no significantly enriched genera once compared with other oral conditions. Their high shares largely reflect that they are sampled in the mouth, where these genera are common in any condition.
- **Decreased:** no condition has a significantly enriched genus.

### Version B: direction within each condition

Asks: *within this condition, is the genus reported in the same direction as in periodontitis more often than in the opposite direction?* This measures how **consistent** the genus's direction is, using the same test as for PerioSigDB in the left panel.

- **First column, "All BugSigDB" (left of the black line):** all BugSigDB studies of either direction, any condition except periodontitis. The label is the number of studies reporting the genus in the figure's direction, out of all studies reporting the genus (a study reporting it in both directions, in different comparisons, counts in both). This shows whether the genus has a consistent direction across the literature in general.
- **Other columns:** BugSigDB conditions, with their total number of studies (both directions) in brackets.
    - Colour is the share of the condition's studies containing the genus that report it in the same direction as periodontitis. Dark orange (increased figure) or dark blue (decreased figure) means consistently the same direction; the opposite colour means consistently the opposite direction; grey-white means mixed.
    - Each cell is tested with an exact binomial test of same vs opposite direction against 50/50, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all genus × condition tests in the figure. Cells with FDR < 0.05 are outlined and bold.
    - Cells based on only 1–2 studies are grey, because a direction can't be judged from so few. White cells mean the genus is not reported in that condition.
- **Which conditions are shown:** the 15 conditions with the most genera significantly in the same direction as periodontitis. Ties are broken by the smallest combined p-values for same-direction genera, among conditions with at least 5 studies.

```{r bsdb-direction-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most consistently increased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and how consistently they are reported as increased within other BugSigDB conditions."
direction_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-direction-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Genera most consistently decreased in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and how consistently they are reported as decreased within other BugSigDB conditions."
direction_heatmap("decreased")
```

**Shows (Version B):**

- **Increased:** within a single condition, only colorectal cancer reaches significance. There the oral pathobionts are reported as increased almost without exception: *Peptostreptococcus* in 27 of 27 studies that report it, *Parvimonas* 24/24, *Porphyromonas* 22/23 and *Fusobacterium* 32/37. Other conditions mostly agree in direction (orange cells) but have too few studies per genus for a significant test.
- **Decreased:** no single condition reaches significance. Across all BugSigDB, *Haemophilus* is significantly more often decreased than increased, matching periodontitis. *Gemella*, *Actinomyces* and *Streptococcus* are significantly more often *increased*, the opposite of periodontitis, so their depletion in periodontitis is not a general pattern.

### Version C: semantic similarity of whole signatures

```{r bsdb-semantic-load}
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R (takes ~20 minutes)
semsim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")
```

Versions A–B work with genera. Versions C and C2 instead compare **whole signatures at the taxa's reported rank**, using semantic similarity on the NCBI taxonomy (as in BugSigDB's own tools), so nothing is collapsed to genus.

- **PerioSigDB consensus signatures:** the taxa, at their reported rank, that PerioSigDB reports significantly more often in one direction than the other (exact binomial test, p < 0.05). That gives `r length(semsim$consensus$increased)` taxa increased ("perio up") and `r length(semsim$consensus$decreased)` decreased ("perio down") in periodontitis, mostly species (e.g. *Porphyromonas gingivalis*, *Tannerella forsythia*; *Streptococcus sanguinis*, *Rothia dentocariosa*).
- **Similarity of a BugSigDB signature to a consensus signature:** each taxon in one is matched with its most similar taxon in the other, and the matches are averaged both ways (best-match average). Taxa are compared by Lin similarity, which is 1 for the same taxon and decreases the further back their closest common ancestor is. So a BugSigDB *Porphyromonas* scores highly against *P. gingivalis*, and a gut *Bacteroides* scores moderately (same order).
- **Direction score:** similarity to the consensus of the **same** direction minus similarity to the **opposite** one. For a BugSigDB increased signature that is (similarity to perio up) − (similarity to perio down); for a decreased signature, (similarity to perio down) − (similarity to perio up). Positive means the signature moves like periodontitis; negative means it looks more like the opposite periodontitis signature.
- **Rank:** each study (disease-vs-control signatures, counted once per study as in the other versions) is ranked by its direction score among all studies of the same direction and body site group, from 0 (lowest) to 1 (highest). This removes the body site and direction effects (e.g. gut decreased signatures generally look more like perio up). A condition's value is the mean rank of its studies; 0.5 is typical for those body sites.
- **Test:** mean rank against 0.5, two-sided Wilcoxon test, Benjamini–Hochberg across all conditions with at least 5 study units. The figure shows the 5 most significant conditions in each direction (same as and opposite to periodontitis), with 95% confidence intervals; filled points have FDR < 0.05.

```{r bsdb-semantic-c}
semsim_dir_units <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
  mutate(score = ifelse(direction == "increased", sim_increased - sim_decreased, sim_decreased - sim_increased)) |>
  summarise(score = mean(score), .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  mutate(rank = (rank(score) - 0.5) / n(), .by = c(direction, site_group)) |>
  filter(n() >= 5, .by = Condition)

semsim_dir <- semsim_dir_units |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    mean_rank = mean(rank),
    ci = 1.96 * sd(rank) / sqrt(n()),
    p = wilcox.test(rank, mu = 0.5, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = Condition
  ) |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-c-fig}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Direction score of BugSigDB conditions: how much more their signatures resemble the periodontitis signature of the same direction than the opposite one, ranked among studies of the same direction and body site group (0.5 = typical). The 5 most significant conditions on each side of 0.5 are shown, most significant at the top, with the number of study units in brackets. Small points: study units, coloured by signature direction; large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval (filled: FDR < 0.05)."
# 5 most significant conditions in each direction, ordered by p-value
c_shown <- semsim_dir |>
  mutate(side = factor(ifelse(mean_rank > 0.5, "Same as periodontitis", "Opposite to periodontitis"),
                       levels = c("Same as periodontitis", "Opposite to periodontitis"))) |>
  slice_min(p, n = 5, by = side) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(Condition, " (", studies, ")\np = ", signif(p, 2), ", FDR = ", signif(fdr, 2)),
         label = fct_reorder(label, -p))

c_points <- inner_join(semsim_dir_units, select(c_shown, Condition, side, label), by = "Condition")

ggplot(c_shown, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_quasirandom(data = c_points, aes(x = rank, color = direction), orientation = "y", width = 0.3, size = 1.1,
                   alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"), name = "Signature",
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), height = 0, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey10") +
  geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = fdr < 0.05), shape = 21, size = 3.5, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_grid(side ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Direction score (rank among studies of the same direction and body site group; 0.5 = typical)", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-c-table}
semsim_dir |>
  filter(p < 0.05) |>
  arrange(p) |>
  transmute(Condition, `Study units` = studies, `Mean rank` = round(mean_rank, 2), p = signif(p, 2), FDR = signif(fdr, 2)) |>
  kbl(caption = "Conditions with p < 0.05 in Version C.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Shows (Version C):**

- **Colorectal cancer** is the only condition significant after FDR correction (mean rank 0.62 over 111 study units): its signatures move like periodontitis more than other studies from the same body sites.
- **Same direction, nominal only:** chronic constipation and cervical glandular intraepithelial neoplasia.
- **Opposite direction, nominal only:** Parkinson's disease, obesity, COVID-19, endometriosis and ulcerative colitis. None passes FDR.
- Most conditions sit close to 0.5, so a periodontitis-like direction is not a generic feature of disease signatures.
- **The study-level points are spread widely**, and the signal in each condition comes from one direction: colorectal cancer's increased signatures (mean rank 0.71; decreased 0.53), Parkinson's disease's and COVID-19's increased signatures (0.41 and 0.37), and obesity's decreased signatures (0.34). Version C2 shows the same split.

Version C2 breaks these results down to see which periodontitis signature drives them, and the tabs below compare the conditions' own consensus signatures with PerioSigDB's.

### Version C2: breakdown by periodontitis signature

Version C's direction score is a difference of two similarities. Version C2 shows the two separately, and for BugSigDB increased and decreased signatures separately, to see which part drives a result: e.g. a condition can score high because its increased taxa look like perio up, or only because they look unlike perio down.

- **Ranks:** each signature is ranked twice among signatures of the same direction and body site group: once by its similarity to perio up (x) and once by its similarity to perio down (y). A condition's point is the mean of its studies' ranks; 0.5 is typical for those body sites.
- **Increased panel:** agreement with periodontitis is **bottom right** (disease-increased taxa resemble periodontitis-increased taxa, not periodontitis-decreased ones).
- **Decreased panel:** agreement is **top left**.
- **Along the diagonal:** the signature resembles both (or neither) equally, e.g. generically oral or generically unrelated, with no direction.
- **Reversed:** the opposite corners (top left in the increased panel, bottom right in the decreased panel).
- Each point is a condition with at least 5 study units in that direction. The two ranks are compared with a paired two-sided Wilcoxon test (equivalent to Version C's test, split by direction). Fill shows whether a difference at p < 0.05 agrees with periodontitis or is reversed. Labelled conditions have p < 0.05; bold labels and dark outlines mark FDR < 0.05 within the panel.

```{r bsdb-semantic-c2}
semsim_c2 <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
  summarise(sim_increased = mean(sim_increased), sim_decreased = mean(sim_decreased),
            .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  mutate(rank_up = (rank(sim_increased) - 0.5) / n(), rank_down = (rank(sim_decreased) - 0.5) / n(),
         .by = c(direction, site_group)) |>
  filter(n() >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    x = mean(rank_up),
    y = mean(rank_down),
    p = wilcox.test(rank_up, rank_down, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(Condition, direction)
  ) |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = direction) |>
  mutate(
    panel = factor(paste("BugSigDB", direction, "signatures"),
                   levels = paste("BugSigDB", c("increased", "decreased"), "signatures")),
    # agreement: increased signatures closer to perio up, decreased closer to perio down
    agrees = ifelse(direction == "increased", x > y, y > x),
    deviation = case_when(
      p >= 0.05 ~ "Not significant",
      agrees ~ "Agrees with periodontitis",
      .default = "Reversed"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("Agrees with periodontitis", "Reversed", "Not significant"))
  )
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-c2-fig}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Similarity of BugSigDB signatures to the periodontitis-increased (x) and periodontitis-decreased (y) consensus signatures, as mean ranks among signatures of the same direction and body site group (0.5 = typical). Agreement with periodontitis is bottom right for increased signatures and top left for decreased signatures."

deviation_colors <- c("Agrees with periodontitis" = "#1baf7a", "Reversed" = "#6250d6", "Not significant" = "grey88")

ggplot(semsim_c2, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_abline(color = "grey80") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(size = studies, fill = deviation, color = fdr < 0.05, stroke = ifelse(fdr < 0.05, 1, 0.3)),
             shape = 21) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = ifelse(p < 0.05, Condition, NA), fontface = ifelse(fdr < 0.05, "bold", "plain")),
                  size = 3.2, color = "grey15", min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = 30, seed = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = deviation_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey5", `FALSE` = "grey50"), guide = "none") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, name = "Study units") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0.1, 0.9), ylim = c(0.1, 0.9)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Similarity to periodontitis-increased signature (mean rank)",
       y = "Similarity to periodontitis-decreased signature (mean rank)")
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-c2-crc}
semsim_c2 |>
  filter(p < 0.05) |>
  arrange(direction, p) |>
  transmute(Direction = direction, Condition, `Study units` = studies,
            `Rank vs perio up` = round(x, 2), `Rank vs perio down` = round(y, 2),
            p = signif(p, 2), FDR = signif(fdr, 2)) |>
  kbl(caption = "Conditions with p < 0.05 in Version C2.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

**Shows (Version C2):**

- **Colorectal cancer** (increased panel) is the only condition significant after FDR correction. Its increased signatures rank high against the periodontitis-increased consensus (0.75) and average against the decreased one (0.49), so the resemblance is direction-specific, not generically oral.
- **Chronic constipation** sits in the same corner (nominal p only). Semantic similarity rewards matches at higher taxonomic ranks, and the periodontitis-increased taxa are mostly anaerobic Bacteroidota and Bacillota, like most gut taxa, so a gut signature can resemble them without sharing oral taxa (see the taxa below).
- **Reversed (nominal p < 0.05, FDR ≈ 0.07–0.09):** obesity's decreased signatures are less like periodontitis-decreased taxa than typical; Parkinson's disease, COVID-19, dry eye syndrome and Crohn's disease have increased signatures that lean towards the periodontitis-*decreased* taxa. None passes FDR.
- **Decreased signatures** show no clear agreement. Atopic eczema is nominal only. Few BugSigDB decreased signatures contain the oral commensals (*Streptococcus*, *Rothia*, *Haemophilus*) that make up the periodontitis-decreased consensus.
- The two axes are measured separately (neither is derived from the other), so a point's distance from the diagonal directly shows direction specificity.

**Caveat:** raw semantic similarity mostly reflects broad taxonomy. For example, in fecal studies BugSigDB's *decreased* signatures are more similar to the periodontitis-*increased* consensus than to the decreased one, because gut taxa are mostly anaerobes like the periodontal pathogens, whereas the periodontitis-decreased taxa are oral aerobes. Ranking within body site group and direction removes most of this, but not all.

#### Consensus signatures of the flagged conditions

For each condition with p < 0.05 in Version C or C2, its own **consensus signatures** are built the same way as for PerioSigDB: taxa, at their reported rank, that the condition's disease-vs-control studies report significantly more often in one direction than the other (exact binomial test, p < 0.05; each study counted once per direction). These are then compared taxon by taxon with the PerioSigDB consensus signatures, in the style of Figure 2c/e of the BugSigDB paper.

- **Heatmap:** rows are the PerioSigDB consensus taxa (periodontitis increased, then decreased), columns are the condition's consensus taxa (increased, then decreased; up to 20 per direction, most significant first), each ordered by taxonomy. The numbers in brackets are studies reporting the taxon increased / decreased. Cells are Lin similarity (1 = same taxon, outlined; about 0.9 = same genus; about 0.5 = same family or order; below about 0.3 = different class or phylum).
- **Reading it:** the top-left (both increased) and bottom-right (both decreased) blocks are agreement with periodontitis; the other two blocks are reversal. Dark cells in an agreement block mean the condition shares those taxa, or close relatives, with periodontitis in the same direction.
- **Similarity of the consensus signatures:** best-match average of each block, as in Version C2.
- Conditions with few studies have few or no consensus taxa: with no discordant studies, a taxon needs at least 6 studies to reach p < 0.05.
- The table under each heatmap gives each condition consensus taxon's closest PerioSigDB taxon.

**Shows:**

- **Colorectal cancer:** 17 taxa form its increased consensus, and several are *identical* to periodontitis-increased taxa (outlined): *Prevotella intermedia*, *Fusobacterium nucleatum*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *P. stomatis* and *Parvimonas micra*. Several others are close relatives (*Porphyromonas*, *P. asaccharolytica*, *Peptostreptococcus anaerobius*). The exception is *Gemella* (and *G. morbillorum*), increased in colorectal cancer but closest to the periodontitis-*decreased* *G. haemolysans*. Its increased consensus resembles periodontitis-increased (0.57) much more than periodontitis-decreased (0.30). Its decreased consensus is only *Faecalibacterium*, unrelated to either.
- **Parkinson's disease:** no taxa are shared. Its increased consensus (*Bifidobacterium*, *Akkermansia*, *Alistipes*) resembles periodontitis taxa only at higher ranks: *Alistipes* is in the same order as *Porphyromonas* and *Tannerella*, and *Bifidobacterium* in the same phylum as *Rothia*, *Actinomyces* and *Corynebacterium*. Its decreased consensus (*Roseburia*, *Blautia*, *Faecalibacterium*, Lachnospiraceae) resembles the periodontitis-*increased* Clostridia (Lachnospiraceae oral taxon 500, *Eubacterium*, *Peptostreptococcus*), which is where its "reversed" score comes from.
