- **The other flagged conditions** have few or no consensus taxa, so their Version C/C2 results rest on scattered taxa that individual studies report rather than a consistent signature.

```{r bsdb-condition-consensus}
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.R
taxon_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.rds")

terminal_id <- function(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", unique(sub("^.*[|]", "", x)))

c2_conditions <- bind_rows(
  semsim_dir |> filter(p < 0.05) |> arrange(desc(mean_rank)) |> select(Condition),
  semsim_c2 |> filter(p < 0.05) |> arrange(deviation, p) |> select(Condition)
) |>
  distinct(Condition) |>
  pull()

# condition consensus signatures, built as for PerioSigDB
condition_tests <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(Condition %in% c2_conditions) |>
  mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
  unnest(taxon) |>
  distinct(Condition, Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(Condition, taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    n = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")
  ) |>
  filter(taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim))

condition_consensus <- filter(condition_tests, p < 0.05)

perio_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(semsim$consensus),
  perio_direction = rep(names(semsim$consensus), lengths(semsim$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(semsim$taxon_tests, id = ids, perio_up = increased, perio_down = decreased), by = "id")

taxon_label <- function(id, up, down) sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", taxon_sim$names[id], up, down)

# best-match average of a block of the similarity matrix
bma <- function(m) if (length(m)) mean(c(apply(m, 1, max), apply(m, 2, max))) else NA

consensus_blocks <- function(cond, n_taxa = 20) {
  cc <- condition_consensus |>
    filter(Condition == cond) |>
    slice_min(p, n = n_taxa, by = direction, with_ties = FALSE)
  m <- taxon_sim$sim[cc$taxon, perio_consensus$id, drop = FALSE]
  tidyr::expand_grid(d = c("increased", "decreased"), pd = c("increased", "decreased")) |>
    mutate(sim = map2_dbl(d, pd, \(d, pd) bma(m[cc$direction == d, perio_consensus$perio_direction == pd, drop = FALSE])))
}

consensus_heatmap <- function(cond, n_taxa = 20) {
  cc <- condition_consensus |>
    filter(Condition == cond) |>
    slice_min(p, n = n_taxa, by = direction, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(label = taxon_label(taxon, increased, decreased))
  pc <- perio_consensus |> mutate(label = taxon_label(id, perio_up, perio_down))

  tidyr::expand_grid(select(pc, id, perio_direction, row = label),
                     select(cc, taxon, direction, col = label)) |>
    mutate(
      sim = taxon_sim$sim[cbind(taxon, id)],
      row = factor(row, levels = rev(pc$label[order(taxon_sim$lineage[pc$id])])),
      col = factor(col, levels = cc$label[order(taxon_sim$lineage[cc$taxon])]),
      perio_direction = factor(paste("Periodontitis", perio_direction),
                               levels = paste("Periodontitis", c("increased", "decreased"))),
      direction = factor(paste(cond, direction), levels = paste(cond, c("increased", "decreased")))
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = col, y = row, fill = sim)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, sim > 0.999), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.6, fill = NA) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f4f4f2", high = "#184f95", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Lin\nsimilarity") +
    facet_grid(perio_direction ~ direction, scales = "free", space = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(14)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 50, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

tint <- function(x, col) rgb(colorRamp(c("white", col))(pmin(x, 1) * 0.55), maxColorValue = 255)

consensus_table <- function(cond, n_taxa = 20) {
  tab <- condition_consensus |>
    filter(Condition == cond) |>
    slice_min(p, n = n_taxa, by = direction, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    left_join(taxon_sim$closest, by = "taxon") |>
    arrange(desc(direction), p) |>
    mutate(
      closer = case_when(sim_up > sim_down ~ "periodontitis-increased",
                         sim_down > sim_up ~ "periodontitis-decreased",
                         .default = "tie"),
      agrees = closer == paste0("periodontitis-", direction),
      closer = paste(closer, ifelse(closer == "tie", "", ifelse(agrees, "&#10003;", "&#10007;")))
    )
  tab |>
    transmute(Taxon = paste0("<i>", name, "</i>"), Direction = direction, `Studies up/down` = paste0(increased, "/", decreased),
              p = signif(p, 2),
              `Closest periodontitis-increased taxon` = paste0("<i>", match_up, "</i>"), `Lin (up)` = sprintf("%.2f", sim_up),
              `Closest periodontitis-decreased taxon` = paste0("<i>", match_down, "</i>"), `Lin (down)` = sprintf("%.2f", sim_down),
              `Closer to` = closer) |>
    kbl(escape = FALSE, align = "lllrlrlrl") |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("condensed"), full_width = TRUE, font_size = 12) |>
    column_spec(6, background = tint(tab$sim_up, "#eb6834")) |>
    column_spec(8, background = tint(tab$sim_down, "#2a78d6")) |>
    as.character()
}
```

```{r bsdb-condition-consensus-tabs}
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 11
cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
for (cond in c2_conditions) {
  cat("##### ", cond, "\n\n", sep = "")
  c_row <- filter(semsim_dir, Condition == cond)
  cat(sprintf("- **Version C** (%d study units): direction score rank %.2f (p = %s, FDR = %s)\n",
              c_row$studies, c_row$mean_rank, signif(c_row$p, 2), signif(c_row$fdr, 2)))
  rows <- semsim_c2 |> filter(Condition == cond) |> arrange(p)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
    r <- rows[i, ]
    cat(sprintf("- **C2, %s signatures** (%d study units): rank %.2f vs periodontitis-increased, %.2f vs periodontitis-decreased; %s (p = %s, FDR = %s)\n",
                r$direction, r$studies, r$x, r$y,
                ifelse(r$p < 0.05, tolower(as.character(r$deviation)), "not significant"),
                signif(r$p, 2), signif(r$fdr, 2)))
  }
  n_cons <- condition_consensus |> filter(Condition == cond) |> count(direction)
  n_of <- function(d) sum(n_cons$n[n_cons$direction == d])
  cat(sprintf("- **Consensus signatures:** %d taxa increased and %d decreased (binomial p < 0.05)\n",
              n_of("increased"), n_of("decreased")))
  if (nrow(n_cons) == 0) {
    cat("\nNo taxa reach p < 0.05; too few studies for a consensus.\n\n")
    next
  }
  blocks <- consensus_blocks(cond)
  sim_of <- function(d, pd) sprintf("%.2f", blocks$sim[blocks$d == d & blocks$pd == pd])
  cat(sprintf("- **Similarity to PerioSigDB consensus (best-match average):** increased vs periodontitis increased %s, vs periodontitis decreased %s; decreased vs periodontitis decreased %s, vs periodontitis increased %s\n\n",
              sim_of("increased", "increased"), sim_of("increased", "decreased"),
              sim_of("decreased", "decreased"), sim_of("decreased", "increased")))
  print(consensus_heatmap(cond))
  cat("\n\n<details><summary>Closest PerioSigDB taxon for each consensus taxon</summary>\n\n")
  cat(consensus_table(cond), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
cat(":::\n\n")
```

### Comparing the versions

- **Version A** finds the most significant cells because it pools the whole database, but it is confounded by body site. Conditions sampled in the mouth look enriched for oral genera partly just because they are oral samples.
- **Version A2** removes that confounding by comparing each condition with others from the same body site group. It is the fairer test of whether a condition is unusual.
- **Version B** compares like with like (the same test as for PerioSigDB) and is not affected by how often a genus is studied or where. However, most conditions have too few studies per genus to reach significance.
- **All three versions single out colorectal cancer, and only colorectal cancer.** *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium* are enriched in its (mostly fecal) studies compared with other gut conditions, and almost always in the same direction as in periodontitis. That is the robust cross-condition finding.
- The apparent links to oral conditions (oral cancer, smoking, rheumatoid arthritis) and to phenylketonuria and cognitive impairment did not survive the body site adjustment or the restriction to disease-vs-control comparisons counted once per study.
- **Versions C and C2** compare whole signatures at the reported rank (species where available), so it uses all the information, but semantic similarity also rewards broad taxonomic resemblance (e.g. any gut anaerobe).
- All versions single out colorectal cancer, and only colorectal cancer, after FDR correction.
- If one version is used, A2 is the most defensible for enrichment, with B and C (broken down by C2) as support for colorectal cancer.

### Suggestive results (not significant)

These results do not survive FDR correction but are biologically coherent and consistent across versions. They were picked after looking at the results, from several hundred tests, so they are hypotheses rather than findings.

```{r bsdb-suggestive}
# selected genus x condition cells: enrichment (Version A2) and direction (Version B)
cell_stats <- function(cond, genus, dir) {
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |> filter(direction == dir, taxon == genus) |> distinct(sig, taxon)
  in_condition <- sigs$Condition == cond
  has_genus <- sigs$sig %in% hits$sig
  reported <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon == genus) |>
    distinct(sig, direction) |>
    left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
    filter(Condition == cond)
  tibble(
    Condition = cond, Genus = genus, `In periodontitis` = dir,
    `Condition studies with genus` = sprintf("%d / %d (%.0f%%)", sum(in_condition & has_genus),
                                             sum(in_condition), 100 * mean(has_genus[in_condition])),
    `All BugSigDB` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(has_genus)),
    `Site-matched p (A2)` = signif(site_matched_p(cond, genus, sigs, hits), 2),
    `Same direction (B)` = sprintf("%d / %d", sum(reported$direction == dir), nrow(reported))
  )
}

tribble(
  ~cond, ~genus, ~dir,
  "Gastric cancer", "Fusobacterium", "increased",
  "Gastric cancer", "Selenomonas", "increased",
  "Colorectal cancer", "Campylobacter", "increased",
  "Colorectal cancer", "Selenomonas", "increased",
  "Colorectal cancer", "Prevotella", "increased",
  "Colorectal cancer", "Dialister", "increased",
  "Rheumatoid arthritis", "Treponema", "increased",
  "Rheumatoid arthritis", "Selenomonas", "increased",
  "Smoking behavior", "Fusobacterium", "increased",
  "Smoking behavior", "Gemella", "decreased",
  "COVID-19", "Neisseria", "decreased"
) |>
  pmap_dfr(cell_stats) |>
  kbl(caption = "Selected genus x condition results. Condition studies with genus: studies of the condition reporting the genus in the same direction as periodontitis. Same direction (B): studies reporting the genus in the same direction as periodontitis, out of all studies of the condition reporting it.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE, font_size = 12)
```

- **Gastric cancer:** *Fusobacterium* is in nearly half of gastric cancer studies, about three times the BugSigDB rate, and almost always increased. This mirrors colorectal cancer on a smaller scale.
- **Colorectal cancer beyond the core four genera:** *Campylobacter*, *Selenomonas*, *Prevotella* and *Dialister* are also more common than in other gut conditions and consistently increased. This broadens the oral-pathobiont pattern.
- **Rheumatoid arthritis:** *Treponema* and *Selenomonas* are enriched and consistently increased, in line with the periodontitis–rheumatoid arthritis link. *Porphyromonas*, the usual candidate, is not singled out.
- **Smoking:** loss of health-associated commensals (*Gemella*, and *Corynebacterium*, *Granulicatella*, *Lautropia* and *Oribacterium* in most studies reporting them) with more *Fusobacterium*. This mirrors periodontitis, for which smoking is a risk factor.
- **COVID-19:** *Neisseria* is consistently decreased, along with other commensals, though mostly in nasopharyngeal and respiratory samples.

**A general disease pattern.** Several PerioSigDB genera have the same direction as in periodontitis in most other conditions, not just a few. The table counts, for each genus, the conditions where most studies report it in the same direction as periodontitis versus the opposite (excluding colorectal cancer; conditions with at least 2 studies reporting the genus).

```{r bsdb-cross-condition}
bsdb_genera |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
  filter(Condition != "Colorectal cancer") |>
  count(Condition, taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio_direction = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(
    same = ifelse(perio_direction == "increased", increased, decreased),
    opposite = ifelse(perio_direction == "increased", decreased, increased)
  ) |>
  filter(same + opposite >= 2) |>
  summarise(conditions = n(), mostly_same = sum(same > opposite), mostly_opposite = sum(opposite > same),
            .by = c(perio_direction, taxon)) |>
  mutate(p = map2_dbl(mostly_same, mostly_same + mostly_opposite,
                      \(k, n) if (n > 0) binom.test(k, n)$p.value else NA_real_)) |>
  filter(p < 0.1) |>
  arrange(p) |>
  transmute(
    Genus = taxon, `In periodontitis` = perio_direction, Conditions = conditions,
    `Mostly same direction` = mostly_same, `Mostly opposite` = mostly_opposite,
    `Sign test p` = signif(p, 2)
  ) |>
  kbl(caption = "Genera with a consistent direction across BugSigDB conditions (sign test p < 0.1).") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12)
```

*Fusobacterium*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Parvimonas* tend to be increased, and *Haemophilus* and *Neisseria* decreased, across many unrelated conditions. So part of the periodontitis signature may reflect a generic disease-vs-health (dysbiosis) pattern rather than anything specifically periodontal. *Streptococcus*, by contrast, is mostly increased elsewhere, the opposite of periodontitis. The sign test treats conditions as independent, although many share studies or populations.


**Caveats:**

- Each study is counted once per condition, direction and body site group, but studies are still treated as independent, and one study can contribute to several conditions.
- The disease-vs-control filter works on group names, so it misses some valid comparisons (e.g. unusual control names) and keeps some that aren't (e.g. a control group defined by an exposure).
- Conditions with few studies can reach significance only for large effects, while large conditions such as colorectal cancer reach it for modest ones.
- Ubiquitous genera (*Prevotella*, *Streptococcus*) appear in many studies regardless of condition. The baseline column helps calibrate.
- The binomial test treats signatures as independent and ignores that PerioSigDB has more increased (`r n_sig_dir[["increased"]]`) than decreased (`r n_sig_dir[["decreased"]]`) signatures. Testing against the observed share of increased signatures instead of 50% would make increased genera slightly less significant and decreased genera slightly more.
- Aggregating PerioSigDB species to genus loses species-level specificity. For example, *Porphyromonas* and *Fusobacterium* appear in both the increased and decreased lists, because different species of each genus move in opposite directions (e.g. *P. gingivalis* up, *P. catoniae* down).

# Summary of options

```{r summary-table}
tribble(
  ~Option, ~Question, ~Form, ~Notes,
  "1. Completeness heatmap", "What metadata are available?", "Heatmap (fields × studies)", "Good supplementary figure; frames all others",
  "2. Paired comparison", "How do health and periodontitis groups differ?", "Paired slopes, small multiples", "Recommended main figure",
  "3. Summary table", "Typical values per group", "Table", "Recommended main table; pairs with 2",
  "4. Pooled effect sizes", "Standardized size of each difference", "Meta-analytic dot plot", "Makes heterogeneity (I²) explicit",
  "5. Severity by classification", "Is 'periodontitis' comparable across studies?", "Beeswarm, small multiples", "Recommended for within-periodontitis variation",
  "6. Trends over time", "Have cohorts changed over time?", "Scatter + trend", "Year confounded with method",
  "7. Classification", "How was periodontitis defined?", "Stacked bars + count tile", "Context for stratification",
  "8. Systemic condition", "Are comorbid populations included?", "Bar chart", "Half not recorded yet",
  "9. Sample size", "How large are studies by method?", "Scatter (log)", "Supports weighting decisions",
  "10. Group imbalance", "Age and smoking confounding", "Scatter with quadrants", "Compact confounding summary",
  "11. Signature content", "Do metadata relate to signatures?", "Scatter + bars", "Exploratory; needs taxa-assessed data",
  "12. Methods and resolution", "How do PerioSigDB and BugSigDB differ structurally?", "Stacked bars", "Explains species vs genus mismatch",
  "13. Metadata fields", "What does each database record?", "Dot matrix", "Shows complementary fields and gaps",
  "14. Taxa across conditions", "Where do periodontitis-linked genera appear elsewhere?", "Heatmaps (A, A2, B) + ranked dots (C) + scatter and taxa tables (C2)", "Most novel; A2 most defensible"
) |>
  kbl(caption = "Candidate figures and tables.") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = TRUE)
```

**Suggested combination:**

- **Main text:** Option 2 (paired comparison) with Option 3 (summary table), plus Option 5 (severity by classification).
- **Supplement:** Option 1 (completeness), with Option 4 or 10 to address confounding.
- **Positioning against BugSigDB:** Option 13 (complementary metadata) and Option 14 (taxa across conditions).
